question: Why can rinsing a sports drink round the mouth and spitting it out improve a one-hour time trial?
answer: Because the mouth reports carbohydrate to the brain. Carter, Jeukendrup and Jones found cyclists rode a one-hour time trial almost 3% faster after rinsing with a carbohydrate solution than with a placebo, though none was swallowed. Brain scans later showed such rinses light up reward areas: the legs work harder when the brain expects fuel.
move: Some signals change behaviour before the thing they announce arrives.
ask: Which small signal changes how I act before the real thing even arrives?
source: Carter et al., Med Sci Sports Exerc, 2004
reference: Carter, Jeukendrup & Jones, The effect of carbohydrate mouth rinse on 1-h cycle time trial performance, Medicine & Science in Sports & Exercise, 2004
